matches.analysis: FEATURED MATCH — first pick since the market-check rule change, and it shows why the extra work matters. Athletic are favourites to win outright (around 1.68), but that price is debated: their derby history with Alavés is remarkably tight, with 12 of the last 13 meetings finishing under 3 goals and both teams scoring in only 39% of them. Athletic tend to win through control, not open exchanges, and Alavés are disciplined defensively even on the back of two straight losses. The goals market, not the win market, is where this fixture's real pattern shows up.

Newcastle are missing five first-team players and have conceded at home in 14 consecutive matches; Hull have scored away in 8 of their last 9 and their in-form striker Bellahmi scored both goals in their last outing. That's exactly the kind of team-news detail that makes a straight home win riskier than the price suggests. BTTS has landed in 9 straight Newcastle home games, and both sides have a live enough attack to make this the cleaner angle.
